title: PR 8142 review scratchpad - kv cache & batching refactor
content:
Quick notes while reviewing PR #8142 (kv-cache + batching refactor). Tossing ideas / TODOs here so I don't forget during sync.

Summary:
- Large refactor that centralizes KV-cache eviction and changes batching behavior for multi-tenant routing.
- Main goals: reduce memory spikes, make batching more deterministic across GPUs, expose new tuning knobs.
- High-level risk areas: correctness of cache invalidation, race conditions on cache population, latency regressions for p99, and test coverage gaps.

High-level impressions:
- Nice cleanup of cache interfaces (CacheManager). Interfaces are clearer but some helper functions are now package-private and used across packages -> might break future imports.
- Batching changes look promising (batch windows aggregated by route key) but I want to see more E2E latency curves (before/after for p50/p95/p99) with representative workload.

Checklist (must-have before merge):
- [ ] Add E2E benchmark run results (perf/latency/cost) for the 3 typical workloads (chat short context, long-context completion, streaming token gen).
- [ ] Unit tests for CacheManager eviction policy edge cases (concurrent insert+evict).
- [ ] Integration test that simulates TTL-based invalidation + model reload to ensure no stale kv cache hits.
- [ ] Add metrics on cache-hit-bytes and cache-eviction-count (tagged by model & route).
- [ ] Verify no semantically visible behavior change for existing consumers (run regression test suite).

File-specific notes:
- cache/manager.go
  - line 134: possible race where entry.refCount is incremented without lock during async prefetch. Suggest wrapping with atomic ops or using mutex held for short window.
  - line 198: eviction loop sleeps for 10ms \u2014 might hide contention; consider event-driven evict on memory pressure + config fallback.
- batching/window.go
  - new BatchWindow aggregator: good idea to use routeKey, but routeKey hashing needs to be stable across processes for Dedicated routing tests. Add comment.
  - window flush logic: flush now triggers on size threshold OR timer; what about interaction with streaming responses? If a stream is started, we should bypass batching for low-latency paths.
- routing/router.go
  - route matching change (fallthrough behavior) could route some requests to slower model variants. Need an explicit canary/annotation to avoid silent routing regressions.

Performance concerns / experiments to run:
- Run 10k qps synthetic with short 16-token prompts, compare token/sec and p99 latency pre/post. Expect ~5-10% throughput improvement but need to confirm no p99 regressions.
- Memory stress test: simulate 100 concurrent model contexts with large KV cache to confirm eviction policy avoids OOM.
- Cold-start tests: ensure first-request latency doesn't spike due to cache warmup blocking main inference thread.

Refactor suggestions (non-blocking):
- Consider moving eviction strategy behind an interface so we can A/B different algorithms (LRU vs size-based vs cost-based). I can follow up with a small RFC if we want to iterate.
- Extract routeKey hashing into util package and add stable hashing for Dedicated (so behavior is identical across nodes).

Follow-ups after merge:
- Add dashboard panels: cache-hit-rate, cache-eviction-rate, batching-window-size distribution (histogram), per-route p99 latency. Assign to observability.
- Post-merge: run canary on Dedicated pool with 2-week sampling, monitor cost regressions.

Questions for author (Lena):
- Did you intentionally make eviction synchronous in the layout for determinism? If so, document rationale in comment.
- Is there a reason we changed route fallthrough ordering vs the old policy? Could be subtle for model variant selection.

Small nit / style:
- A few files use tab indent vs spaces (e.g., cache/manager_test.go). Standardize to 2-space per repo style.
- Rename BatchWindow.Flush -> FlushIfReady to make side-effects clearer (minor).

Testing notes:
- Unit tests added are good but missing negative tests for concurrent evict+insert. I sketched one locally (will paste into a follow-up comment if needed).
- Need to add a flaky-test guard around integration that uses real GPUs \u2014 use test tag `integration_gpu` and gate on CI label.

Potential bug I found (proof-of-concept):
- Repro steps: run local simulated workload with two workers, each prefetches the same context token sequence, then kill one worker mid-prefetch. Observed double-free on entry in logs (stack trace points to manager.evictEntry). Hypothesis: refCount decrement happens twice because abort path doesn't clear prefetch inflight flag.
- Suggested fix: add inflight map with mutex + ensure abort path clears flag before decrementing refCount. Also assert refCount never goes negative in tests.

Action items for me:
- [ ] Add concurrency unit test for evict+insert. (ETA: 1 day)
- [ ] Run perf suite on staging (small/medium/large) and attach results. (ETA: 2 days)
- [ ] Draft small RFC for eviction strategies if results show tradeoffs. (ETA: next week)

Comments I'll leave on PR: concise versions of above

- point out race, request benchmarks, and ask for eviction/inflight handling to be hardened. Also ask author to call out decision on route fallthrough in PR description.

Misc references and links:
- Similar discussion from last year on cache eviction: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6120 (notes in PR)
- Related Jira: JIRA-OPS-398 (OOM incident that motivated current change)

End notes:
- This is a pretty reasonable refactor. If the race/eviction concerns are addressed and perf is validated, I am +1.

Random quick ideas (brain dump):
- Expose a "prefetch priority" hint in requests to allow prefetching of hot contexts only.
- Add a tiny adaptive timer: if flush rate is low, increase window a bit to improve batch size; otherwise decrease.

-- Aisha
